notes:
Fix the reorderable before-after set (dusk/dawn don't bracket the same span as seed/wilt); tighten object-component's weaker pair (thorn vs rhizome). Leave the other two sets untouched.
- set-before-after: dusk/dawn don't bookend 'the night' as claimed, and the pair is ambiguously reversible against seed/wilt (seed:dawn::wilt:dusk reads just as well), making the set reorderable/ambiguous.
  Try: Replace dusk/dawn with a pair that has a clear, non-reversible directional span matching seed→wilt (e.g., sunrise:sunset, birth:death), chosen so the earlier/later mapping to seed/wilt is unambiguous
  Or: Reframe the relationship to remove directionality entirely if a strictly non-reversible replacement can't be found, and adjust the paradigm accordingly
  Or: Editor wants further research into why this ordering issue occurs before locking a fix — flag for deeper analysis rather than a quick swap
- set-object-component: Thorn is not a universal/defining feature of roses (many are thornless) while rhizome is a necessary feature of all irises — the two pairs aren't equally strong instances of 'a feature it simply has.'
  Try: Replace rose/thorn with a flower:feature pair where the feature is as universal/defining as rhizome-to-iris (e.g., dandelion:taproot, sunflower:receptacle)
  Or: Replace iris/rhizome with a pair matching thorn's optional-but-iconic grain (e.g., holly:spine) if the editor prefers keeping rose
  Or: Per style-guide evocativeness note, consider less-expected flowers (e.g., peony, dahlia) when selecting the replacement pair, since a new pair is being sourced anyway
Do not change: set-location-product, set-agent-instrument — these were approved.
